title: Displacement protection is increasingly constrained by funding flexibility, operational capacity, legal access, and the ability to connect aid to work and local systems
geography: UNHCR global protection and assistance operations in 2025, including refugee, asylum-seeker, internally displaced, returnee, and stateless populations

observations.period: 2025; global humanitarian need and available resources

denominator.unit: forcibly displaced and stateless people UNHCR aimed to protect and assist worldwide in 2025

people_targeted.unit: forcibly displaced and stateless people targeted for protection and assistance in 2025

funds_available.unit: US dollars available to UNHCR in 2025

funding_coverage.unit: percent of total needs covered by available funding in 2025

funding_change.unit: US-dollar change in available resources from 2024 to 2025

observations.method: UNHCR global operational and financial reporting on target populations, needs, available resources, expenditures, and results for 2025.
observations.uncertainty: A target population and funding-coverage ratio do not measure each person's receipt, adequacy, protection quality, unmet need, or the counterfactual effect of additional funds.
observations.subgroup: Refugees, asylum-seekers, internally displaced people, returnees, stateless people, host communities, national partners, donors, and UNHCR operations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Operational prioritization, national systems, community-based delivery, cash assistance, and partnerships can preserve protection despite funding contraction; aggregate coverage does not show where capacity was preserved or lost.

denominator.unit: UNHCR global operating footprint and workforce frame

emergencies_managed.unit: emergencies managed by UNHCR in 16 countries during 2025

people_assisted.unit: forcibly displaced and stateless people assisted by UNHCR in 2025

assistance_change.unit: percent change in people assisted compared with 2024

workforce_change.unit: positions reduced by January 2026, more than

observations.method: UNHCR comparison of emergency operations, assistance reach, expenditure, and workforce footprint across reporting years.
observations.uncertainty: People assisted and workforce counts describe organizational reach, not the quality, continuity, or outcomes of protection services; changes can reflect prioritization, reporting, caseload composition, or delivery through partners.
observations.subgroup: Displaced people seeking protection and services, frontline staff, national and community partners, host institutions, and local service systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reduced direct presence may coexist with more efficient partner delivery, national-system integration, or improved targeting, while a smaller footprint can also reduce access in under-covered crises.

observations.period: 2025; funding flexibility, earmarking, and allocation capacity

denominator.unit: US dollars of UNHCR funds available in 2025

funding_gap.unit: percent gap between UNHCR's 2025 budgeted needs and available funds

tightly_earmarked_share.unit: percent of UNHCR's overall funding portfolio that was tightly earmarked in 2025

tightly_earmarked_change.unit: percent increase in tightly earmarked funding from 2024 to 2025

allocation_constraint.value: reduced flexibility to allocate resources to urgent and unforeseen needs, including crises receiving limited media or donor attention

observations.method: UNHCR financial reporting on budgeted needs, available resources, donor earmarking, expenditure, and allocation flexibility.
observations.uncertainty: Earmarking is not inherently ineffective, and a funding gap does not identify which people or services would have benefited from flexible funds; the mechanism is an organizational allocation constraint, not a direct welfare estimate.
observations.subgroup: Displaced people in high-visibility and under-covered crises, UNHCR country operations, donors, implementing partners, and host-country institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Tightly earmarked funds can protect donor priorities, support accountability, and finance specified services; flexible resources can also be difficult to govern or prioritize without clear allocation rules.

observations.period: 2025; protection, legal status, work access, and durable pathways

denominator.unit: UNHCR protection, livelihood, legal-access, and durable-solutions program frame

protection_services.unit: people receiving protection services in 137 countries in 2025

legal_work_policy_case.unit: refugees from nine camps in Thailand covered by a 2025 policy allowing access to jobs across much of the country

resettlement_departures.unit: refugees supported by UNHCR to depart for resettlement in third countries in 2025, more than

pathway_mechanisms.value: legal work, documentation, cash assistance, national education and health systems, resettlement, complementary pathways, and local integration

observations.method: UNHCR results reporting across protection services, legal aid, work-access policy, resettlement, complementary pathways, and local integration.
observations.uncertainty: Service reach, policy coverage, and departures do not establish individual receipt, safety, income adequacy, family reunification, durable integration, or equal access across displaced populations.
observations.subgroup: Refugees, asylum-seekers, internally displaced people, children, women, people with specific needs, host communities, employers, national authorities, and legal-service providers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Legal work and national-system access can widen autonomy and reduce aid dependence, while documentation, discrimination, geographic separation, and limited quotas can leave formal pathways inaccessible to many.

related_sources.claim: UNHCR Global Trends 2025 population statistics provide the displacement context for the operational report.
UNHCR funding updates provide donor and contribution context for the 2025 financial results.

boundary: This record adds a displacement-to-protection-capacity-to-access route linking humanitarian funding, earmarking, staffing, legal status, work access, national systems, and durable pathways. It is not respondent-level data, an individual service-receipt file, a causal estimate of funding effects, or proof that formal access became safe, adequate, durable, or equally distributed.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UNHCR Global Report 2025 page was reviewed; target population, funding, coverage, emergency operations, assistance reach, workforce change, earmarking, protection services, work-access policy, resettlement, and institutional-boundary claims were cross-checked.
